title: Table walk (ITERATION-FUNCTION.md section 4) against the shipping sigma walk, RTX PRO 4500

host.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition
host.note: The target RTX PRO 6000 (g7e) could not be allocated: every launch attempt in us-east-1 and us-west-2 returned VcpuLimitExceeded because the running worker fleet holds the G-family vCPU quota. Every 6000 figure in ITERATION-FUNCTION.md section 6 is an extrapolation from this host and is marked as such.

preset: BATCH=16 THREADS=256 MINBLOCKS=2 PACKED_SINGLE_PRODUCT=1 PACKED_CACHE_DENOM=1 PACKED_BY_VALUE=1 PACKED_PERM_SIGMA=3 PACKED_POLY_CHAIN=1 PACKED_UNROLL_INV=1 PACKED_PAIR_PRODUCTS=1 PACKED_POLY_STATE=1 PACKED_DIRECT_REDUCE=1 PACKED_GENERATED_PRODUCT=1 PACKED_CLMAD=1 PACKED_STATE_TILE=256 PACKED_WEIGHTED_PREFIX=2 PACKED_COMPACT_STATE=1 PACKED_SHARED_SIGMA=1

commands.unitTest: make test-table-walk-cuda <preset> (runs build/test-table-walk-cuda: 4096 device points against the host reference)
commands.clock: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks.sm,power.draw,temperature.gpu sampled immediately after each bench

tablePlanes.knobs: WALK_TABLE=1 TABLE_BRANCHES=8 (bit-plane selection, superseded by the LUT selection in the same PR)
tablePlanes.costing: raw/kernel-cost-table-planes.txt (predates the quarter-rate column; 2147.2 is the same SASS re-priced with POPC/FLO at 3.97 slots)

tableLut.selection: byte LUT for the phase, nibble LUT for the pivot, 48,508 shared bytes per block

verify300.note: identical iteration count per run; DP rate identical within 0.12%, the dpWeight predicate is unchanged

benchmark.unit: B scalar updates / s, --bench, 1024 steps x 32 launches, --verify 0

updatesPerSmClock.formula: median B/s / (82 SMs x median clock)

benchmark.powerNote: The 4500 sits at its 165 W limit in both kernels; the table kernel draws more per clock and is clocked 6.6% lower, so its fixed-power gain (8.7%) is smaller than its per-clock gain (16.4%). The per-clock figure is the one that transfers to a GPU with power headroom.

extrapolationRtxPro6000BeforeMeasurement.marked: EXTRAPOLATION made before the 6000 was available; retained as the 'before' mark, superseded by rtxPro6000 below

host.instance: g7e.2xlarge (us-east-1b, i-042094f5d76f96ccb), launched 11:25 UTC after the vCPU quota freed
host.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition
host.preset: same knobs as the 4500 run; binaries rebuilt on the host by gpujob.sh

instructionRatesLanesPerSecond.note: within 1% of the 4500 on every stream; the clmad ratio 1/37.7 assumed in ITERATION-FUNCTION.md section 1 is confirmed at 1/38.0

verify300.firstAttempt: dp-weight 50 with the default 65,536-record buffer overflowed on 188 SMs (125,865 / 126,331 reports) and aborted with exit 7 before verifying anything: raw/rtx6000-verify-dp50-overflow.log. The dp-weight 48 rerun above is the accepted check.

benchmark.unit: B scalar updates / s, --bench --steps 1024 --launches 32 --verify 0, automatic worker count (96,256 threads)
benchmark.powerNote: both kernels stay under the 600 W limit (legacy ~520 W, table ~555 W); the table kernel gives up 1.1% of clock, so the fixed-power and per-clock gains nearly coincide here, unlike on the 165 W 4500

rtxPro6000.auditedGeometry: see auditedGeometry385k below (added by the follow-up job)

auditedGeometry385k.unit: B scalar updates / s, --bench --threads 385024 --steps 1024 --launches 32 --verify 0 (RTX_PRO6000_WORKERS, the audited preset's geometry, four times the automatic count)
auditedGeometry385k.note: Oversubscribing 4x lifts the shipping kernel 4% (14.41 -> 14.98; the audited 14.64 sits between the two geometries) while the table kernel loses 1.3% (16.56 -> 16.35): per SM-clock it gains 2.8% but the card clocks it 3.9% lower. Power samples after each run read 547-555 W; the run itself is likely at the 600 W limit. The gain therefore depends on geometry: +14.9% at the automatic worker count, +9.2% at 4x. Best table configuration against best shipping configuration: 16.56 / 14.98 = 1.105.

target.verdict: NOT MET in either geometry: engineering that did not pay by the pre-declared rule; the shipping walk stays the campaign default
